_readme: WHAT MACHINE IS IT (SOUNDS, 9/24/26) -- row [analog horror sound], round two. DIRECTION's bible rule 8 is DIEGETIC OR DEAD: static, scanlines, tape damage and drop-outs live ONLY inside in-world screens and speakers, and the lens is an eye. That ruling decides which of the school page's ten rules can be asked of which sound, so every sound the game ships is classified here ONCE, and nowhere else. This is a CLASSIFICATION, never a verdict: gates/analog_horror_sound_gate.js measures each sound against the rules its class allows and works the verdict out from the numbers. Adding a sound to the game without adding it here turns that gate red on purpose, so a new sound cannot enter without somebody saying what it came off.

ear.why: heard with your own ears in the open air or in a room. NO MACHINE, so rule 4 does not apply to it and rules 5 and 6 are FORBIDDEN on it: a footfall under your own boot has no tape to wobble and no oxide to lose contact. What it owes is a real transient with real top end (rule 3), a floor that is never digital zero (rule 1), and peaks that round off (rule 8).
ear.transientWhy: TWO HARD THINGS TOUCHING. A boot on concrete, brass on a floor, a magazine seating: the contact is a step change in air pressure and a step change is broadband by definition, so a version of it with nothing above 500 Hz is a filtered tone and not a recording of the event. Marked per sound rather than guessed from the name, and NOT marked on the sounds that are a body or the air (a heart, lungs, wind at night, the hit you take), which are genuinely low and must not be dragged upward to satisfy a checker.

hum.why: a machine you can walk up to and point at: a generator, a transformer, a lit sign. Heard directly, so no tape damage, but rule 2 binds it -- a live circuit in North America hums at 60 Hz or an integer multiple of it, and a dead one does not hum at all.

speaker.why: it reaches you through a device that reproduces or transmits. This is the ONE class where the band, the hiss, the wobble and the drop-outs belong by right rather than by taste, and the one class rule 4 can be asked of.

handset.why: the phone in his pocket, which is where every interface sound in this game really comes from: a telephone line is 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz and a handset speaker is no better

am.why: an AM broadcast: 10 kHz channel spacing leaves 5 kHz of audio, which is why a transmitted voice sounds boxed in

cassette.why: a good deck with the right tape

buzz_more.note: the phone's own buzzer is a motor against a case, not a speaker

heartbeat.note: your own body, which is as direct as a sound gets

phone_buzz.note: the buzz is the motor; the phone's TONE is a speaker and is a separate cooked sound

power_on.note: THE BLOCK LIGHTS: a circuit coming alive, which is rule 2's whole subject

save_chime.note: SAVED. Nothing in the world makes this noise, which is exactly what rule 8 calls dead: it has to come out of the phone or not exist

sign_alive.note: a neon transformer, and a transformer's pitch is the grid's pitch

tape_more.note: ADHESIVE tape, patching yourself up, NOT magnetic tape. Named here because the word invites exactly the wrong rule

tape_pull.note: the same: YOU PATCH YOURSELF UP

time_pass.note: HOURS GO BY. An abstraction with no body, which rule 8 forbids: it belongs to a clock, a chime or a broadcast you can point at

ui_deny.note: and rule 23 gives this one a job: a refused press has to say WHY, out of the device in his hand
